title: OpenAI's quarterly revenue reportedly passes $10 billion for the first time

blocks.text: TechCrunch reports that OpenAI's quarterly revenue has crossed $10 billion for the first time. That is almost 50% more than the $6.7 billion the company recorded in the second quarter.
Why it matters
The figure suggests how quickly paying demand for AI products is growing. It also gives a rough gauge of the company's scale as it competes in a costly industry.
OpenAI is the company behind ChatGPT. It is privately held, so it does not publish regular financial reports like listed companies do. Figures about its finances often come from media reports.

title: Georgia moves to No. 1 in College Football Playoff rankings, ahead of Miami

blocks.text: Georgia rose to No. 1 in the latest College Football Playoff rankings, released Tuesday night. It replaced Miami at the top. Notre Dame jumped six places to No. 5.
Why it matters
These rankings signal how the selection committee currently views each team. Top-ranked teams are in the best position for a playoff berth, though the rankings change weekly.

The College Football Playoff is the postseason tournament that decides the US top-level college football champion. A selection committee publishes rankings through the late season, and the final ones set the playoff field.

title: Johns Hopkins tool puts cost of 2025 U.S. measles outbreak at over $37 million

blocks.text: CNBC reports that measles is surging in the U.S. A new tool from Johns Hopkins researchers estimates the 2025 outbreak carried an economic cost of more than $37 million.
Why it matters
Putting a dollar figure on an outbreak shows that costs reach beyond patients. Local health departments and communities also bear them. Such estimates can help officials plan responses.
Measles is a highly contagious viral disease that spreads through the air. It can be prevented with a vaccine. Outbreaks typically require contact tracing and public health response work.

title: Fed's Goolsbee calls October inflation report 'borderline disturbing' as officials weigh more rate hikes

blocks.text: The consumer price index rose more than expected in October, according to CNBC. Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago president Austan Goolsbee called the report 'borderline disturbing'. The reporting says the central bank is weighing more rate hikes.
Why it matters
Inflation that runs hotter than forecast can push the Fed toward raising borrowing costs further. That can affect mortgages, car loans, credit cards and business lending.

The Fed is the U.S. central bank. It aims to keep prices stable and employment high, and it mainly does so by setting a short-term interest rate. The consumer price index tracks how much prices change for a typical basket of goods and services.

title: India cuts visa categories from 13 to 9 and trims application paperwork

blocks.text: India has simplified its visa rules. The number of visa categories falls from 13 to 9, and the application form is made about 70% leaner, according to The Hindu, The Indian Express and The Times of India.
Why it matters
Fewer categories and less paperwork can make it easier for travellers, students, workers and businesses to work out which visa they need and to apply.
A visa is official permission to enter a country for a stated purpose, such as tourism, work or study. Each category carries its own rules and documents.

title: India's net direct tax collections rise 11.8% to ₹14.42 trillion so far in FY27

blocks.text: India's net direct tax collections rose 11.76% to ₹14.42 trillion by 10 November in FY27, according to Mint. Corporate tax receipts led the growth, rising 17.8%. Faster refunds moderated the growth in net collections.
Why it matters

Direct tax receipts are a key source of government revenue and a rough gauge of how incomes and company profits are doing. Faster refunds lower the net figure but put money back with taxpayers sooner.

Direct taxes are levied on incomes and profits, such as personal income tax and corporate tax. Net collections are the amount left after refunds are paid out. FY27 is the financial year running from April 2026 to March 2027.

title: Cabinet approves Rs 2,390 crore Aqua Line extension to Greater Noida Sector 4

blocks.text: The Union Cabinet has approved extending the Noida metro line from Noida Sector 51 to Greater Noida Sector 4. The Indian Express puts the cost at Rs 2,390 crore.
Why it matters
According to The Hindu, once the corridor opens, Noida and Greater Noida will have 71.88 km of active metro network. The phase aims to link key zones of Noida, including commercial hubs.

The Aqua Line is the metro line serving Noida and Greater Noida, which are neighbouring cities in Uttar Pradesh near Delhi. Cabinet approval is a formal step toward building a project, not its completion.

title: India and France hold dialogue on economic security and critical technologies

blocks.text: India and France held the India-France Economic Security and Critical Technologies Dialogue. The two sides discussed supply chain vulnerabilities, critical technologies, cybersecurity and safeguarding strategic supplies. Space and technology were also on the agenda.
Why it matters
Supply chains and key technologies are areas where countries seek to reduce dependence on single suppliers. Talks like this show where the two governments may cooperate.
India and France have a long-standing strategic partnership that covers defence, space and technology. A dialogue of this kind is a formal discussion, not a binding agreement.

title: Kenya discharges last Ebola patient and starts 42-day countdown to ending outbreak

blocks.text: Kenya has discharged its last Ebola patient. This starts a 42-day countdown to being declared Ebola-free, provided no new cases appear. Kenya had nine confirmed cases in total.
Why it matters

It is a milestone toward ending the outbreak in Kenya. Health Minister Aden Duale said prevention measures will continue until December 23. Meanwhile, DR Congo is still fighting what DW calls its deadliest outbreak of the disease.

Ebola is a severe viral illness that spreads through contact with bodily fluids. An outbreak is typically declared over after 42 days, twice the disease's maximum incubation period, without new cases.

title: Spain holds first general strike in 14 years over housing costs

blocks.text: Workers across nearly all industries joined a general strike in Spain, the first in 14 years. Reports say it caused widespread disruption, with protests expected in the biggest cities. Soaring rents and a worsening housing shortage are driving it, alongside concerns about wages.
Why it matters

Housing is the main political debate ahead of Spain's parliamentary elections on November 29, less than three weeks away. A strike of this scale puts the issue in front of voters and parties at a sensitive moment.
A general strike is a walkout across many sectors at once, not just one industry. It is a rare and significant form of protest.

title: Russia and Ukraine agree to prisoner swap after Abu Dhabi talks

blocks.text: Russia and Ukraine agreed to a major prisoner exchange after U.S.-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates. Al Jazeera reports these were the first talks between the two sides since February.
Why it matters
Prisoner swaps are among the few areas where the two sides have been able to reach agreements. Direct talks resuming after months may signal some channel for dialogue remains open.
Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Both countries have held prisoners of war, and exchanges have occurred periodically during the conflict.

title: Indonesia's vice president resigns as ruling alliance shows strain

blocks.text: Indonesia's vice president has resigned. The BBC says this comes as signs grow that the ruling alliance is fraying. It also comes as President Prabowo faces a growing rift with his predecessor, Joko Widodo.
Why it matters
A vice president's exit and a split between a president and his predecessor could shift political balance in Indonesia, the world's third-largest democracy.
Prabowo Subianto is Indonesia's president. Joko Widodo, often called Jokowi, led the country before him.
